label: token right after an early y (pos 2-3), esp. after k-y or y-then-2
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.004% of steps). It fires in the original phase almost only at t=2 or t=3, on the step right after the input y (prev_tok=y accounts for 99.9% of activation mass). Two sub-contexts dominate: the bigram k y before t=3 (prev2=k, 70% of mass) and the input 2 right after y (55% of mass). The strongest activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) are sequences that start b k y or b j y / b b y. With first token u, h, 3 or y, activations are weaker (0.1-0.4). y y 2 gives about 0.13. It never fires in the copy phase or at t>=5, and it does not fire after y later in the sequence. Precision is low: most early post-y steps that match these contexts stay silent, so the firing depends on a specific combination of the first tokens that no simple predicate captures. The predicate gets high mass recall but low precision.
